reads.found: CHECKED ZERO at the foot of both columns, both apparatus layers (no numbered conjecture, no asterisk or letter key). FOUR [var:] SITES CONFIRMED AS MIGNE'S TYPE. (1) 0250A 'Primum mandatum ergo est : Non erunt tibi dii alii praeter me.' -- the Decalogue's FIRST precept, against Ex 20:3 'Non habebis deos alienos coram me'. This is the divergence ADJUDICATIONS section 2 records as unmarked at 0205B; it recurs six times in chunk 0025 and is marked once, at its first occurrence here. (2) 0250C 'Non facies tibi idolum, neque ullam similitudinem' against Ex 20:4 'Non facies tibi sculptile, neque omnem similitudinem'; Origen's whole exposition distinguishes idolum from similitudo. (3) 0250D 'et Deus Deo locutus est' against Ps 49:1 'Deus deorum Dominus locutus est' -- the verse is adduced to show Scripture NAMING GODS in the plural, which Migne's singular does not do. (4) 0250D 'Cum divideret Excelsus gentes et separabat filios Adam, statuit terminos gentium secundum numerum angelorum Dei' against Dt 32:8 'juxta numerum filiorum Israel'; the reading is the Septuagint's and every line of the following argument stands on it. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: 'domus liberalitatis' at 0249D (a real word, and Migne prints 'domus libertatis' three times around it -- rendered literally, no marker); 'Ego sum Dominus Deus tuus qui eduxi te terra Aegypti' at 0249D, WITHOUT the preposition 'de' that the full form at 0250A carries; the whole Jn 8:31-32 quotation; 'Gal. iv', 'Joan. viii', 'Deut. xxxii', 'Col. i.' in lowercase roman as our twin's capitals render them. OBSERVATION NOT ACTED ON: the plate's 'VERS 3.' at 0250C shows no period after VERS, where our twin has 'VERS. 3.--'. The mark is a single fine point and this book is demonstrably under-inked in places; left as an open observation, not a patch.

reads.found: CHECKED ZERO at the foot of both columns, both apparatus layers. ONE [var:] SITE AND ONE IMPORTANT NEGATIVE. (1) 0254A CONFIRMED, a [var:] site: 'Visitabo in virga iniquitates eorum, etc., misericordiam autem meam non auferam ab eis.' against Ps 88:34 'misericordiam autem meam non dispergam ab eo' -- a different verb, and Migne's PLURAL is what carries the mercy to the sons, which is the argument. (2) 0254A, THE NEGATIVE, and it is the class the 0005-0009 stint's four withdrawals belong to: our twin prints 'omnia enim ei servantur in futurum. unde Matth. VIII): Quid venisti ante tempus torquere nos?' -- a full stop followed by a LOWERCASE unde, and an UNMATCHED closing parenthesis after the numeral. THE PLATE SETS ALL THREE EXACTLY SO. They are Migne's, not ours: no [sic:], no TEI patch, Pattern 8 preserves them and the English carries the stop and the lowercase. CONFIRMED AND DECLINED: 0254A 'Non vult Deus mortem peccatoris, sed ut magis convertatur et vivat (Ezech. xxxiii)' -- the current liturgical short form of Ez 33:11, no argument turns on it. 0254C 'in quibus tota lex pendet et prophetae (Matth. xxii)' against Mt 22:40 'In his duobus mandatis universa lex pendet' -- Migne's relative is his own adaptation to the sentence. 0254D 'Auferam cor lapideum, et dabo eis cor carneum' cited as Ezech. xxxvi but agreeing with Ez 11:19's 'eis' rather than Ez 36:26's 'vobis' -- his citation, recorded only. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: the whole Isidore precept-list at 0254C, word for word; 'Non in tabulis lapideis, sed in tabulis cordis carnalibus'; the Origen Old-Latin prophets at 0253A-B (Isa. l 'Propter iniquitates vestras dimisit matrem vestram', Jer. iii 'Nunquid mulier si exierit a viro', Jer. vi 'Dolore et flagello castigaberis, Hierusalem'), declined as a class.

reads.found: ⭐⭐ NOT A CHECKED ZERO -- THIS LEAF CARRIES A FOOT-OF-PAGE NOTE LAYER THAT OUR TEI HAS DROPPED ENTIRELY. At 0256C the plate keys a raised letter 'a' to the last words of the Isidore gloss ('omnes unum altare faciunt in unitate fidei et concordia charitatis a.'), and the foot of the page carries a long two-column editorial note, in smaller type, on the division of the Decalogue -- Augustine's enumeration, the scholastic doctors who follow it, and Origen's conjoining of the two prohibitions of concupiscence ('Augustini autem enumerationem eo sensu sequuntur doctores scholastici, quo ipsemet Augustinus... Rursus illas duas concupiscentiae duplicis prohibitiones in unum praeceptum conjicit Origenes, propter consequentiam contextus...'). The note RUNS OVER onto the foot of f129. Our twin carries neither the raised key nor a word of the note. Under Pattern 19 this is the letter-keyed layer (8950's class) and takes both a Latin [cn: a | ...] and a translated English [nt: ...], because it is prose, not a reading. Recovery is per VOLUME at chunking and is NOT done here; the site is filed in 8949-PENDING-TEI-PATCHES-0025.md. ⛔ This DISPROVES, for this book, the inherited PL 113 'no foot-of-page apparatus' spot-check zero. ONE [var:] SITE AND ONE WITHDRAWAL. (1) 0255A CONFIRMED, a [var:] site: 'Non concupisces uxorem proximi tui?' -- a commentary on Exodus 20 quoting Dt 5:21's wording, not Ex 20:17's 'Non concupisces domum proximi tui, nec desiderabis uxorem ejus'. Same class as the 0010-0014 stint's 0215D finding. (2) 0255A WITHDRAWAL of nothing, but the control matters: THE PLATE PRINTS THE OE LIGATURE FOUR TIMES on this column -- 'Non moechaberis', 'non moechaberis' twice, 'moechandi', 'moechetur' -- exactly as ADJUDICATIONS section 3 warns, and our twin has 'oe' correctly here. No Decalogue verb was fired on. (3) 0256B CONFIRMED and declined: 'Simulacra gentium argentum et aurum, opera manum hominum' against Ps 113:12 'opera manuum hominum'. Real word, no sense change, below the Pattern 14 bar. (4) 0256C CONFIRMED, a [var:] site: 'Vos estis lapides vivi, coaedificati in domos spirituales' against 1 Pt 2:5 'et ipsi tamquam lapides vivi superaedificamini, domus spiritualis' -- indicative for imperative and plural houses for a single house, in a gloss whose whole point is unity. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: 0255B '(AUG., ubi supra.)' with a PERIOD -- our twin's trailing ', )' is OURS, filed as a patch; 'Non furtum facies' at 0255B, the Vulgate form of Ex 20:15, which is the internal control showing that Rabanus's 'Non furaberis' at 0211A is a distinct short form and not a compositor's slip; 'VERS. 21, 22.', 'VERS. 24.', 'VERS. 25, 26.'; 'Cunc'us' at 0255C is a worn t, not a defect.

reads.found: NOT A CHECKED ZERO -- the foot of this leaf carries the CONTINUATION of the letter-keyed Decalogue-division note begun on f128 ('Non concupisces domum proximi tui, nec desiderabis uxorem ejus, neque, etc. Augustinus autem eas in duo praecepta divisit... licet ambigas faciant ne verba illa unam an duas leges.'). Our twin carries none of it; filed with the f128 site. ONE MAJOR [var:] SITE. 0258A CONFIRMED as Migne's type, in full: '(ORIG., hom. 10 in Exod.) Quod si litigabunt duo viri, et percusserint mulierem praegnantem, et exierit infans ejus nondum formatus, detrimentum patietur, quantum indixerit vir mulieris, et dabit pro anima sua. Quod si formatus fuerit, dabit animam pro anima, oculum pro oculo, etc.' The Vulgate's Ex 21:22-23 has no formed/unformed distinction at all ('et abortivum quidem fecerit, sed ipsa vixerit: subjacebit damno...'); the reading is the Septuagint's, and BOTH the Augustine quaestio immediately above it and the whole of Origen's exposition below it are about nothing else. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: 'VERS. 1. 6. --' at 0257A, with a PERIOD between the two numerals where every neighbouring head has a comma or a dash -- MIGNE'S OWN, no patch; '(AUG., loc. 91 in Exod.)'; '(AUG., quaest. 77 in Exod.)'; '(I Petr. ii)'; 'Sex annis.'; 'quantum' with the plate's macron for the final m. CONFIRMED AND DECLINED at 0258C: 'Vides festucam in oculo fratris tui, et trabem quae in oculo tuo est non vides' (Mt 7:3 is a question and lacks 'quae... est'); 'Nolite contendere verbis' for 2 Tim 2:14's singular 'Noli' -- the plural is the adaptation to the two litigants and is the point; 'Quaestiones legis devita, sciens quod generant lites', a conflation of 2 Tim 2:23 with Tit 3:9 under Migne's own 'ibidem'.

reads.found: CHECKED ZERO at the foot of both columns, both apparatus layers. FOUR [var:] SITES AND ONE READING LEFT OPEN. (1) 0259B CONFIRMED: 'Si cujus opus arserit damnum patietur, etc.' against 1 Cor 3:15 'detrimentum patietur'. The exposition around it uses Migne's word five times -- 'Damnum ergo patietur, qui excussit. De damnis ergo doctorem dicit Apostolus', 'quaedam peccata ad damnum pertinent', 'qui damnum passus fuerit', 'damno dicitur percuti' -- so conforming the lemma would take the keyword out of its own proof-text. Pattern 7a''s founding shape. (2) 0259B CONFIRMED: 'Quid prodest homini si universum mundum lucretur, animam autem suam perdat?' against Mt 16:26 'animae vero suae detrimentum patiatur'. ⚑ Both quotations in this one paragraph are adjusted AWAY from 'detrimentum' and toward damnum/perdat, which is what makes them a pair rather than two slips. (3) 0260B CONFIRMED: 'Vae praegnantibus et nutrientibus in illis diebus, in quibus scandalizabuntur, si fieri potest, etiam electi' -- Mt 24:19 ends at 'in illis diebus'; the rest is Mt 24:24 welded on with a relative 'in quibus' that neither verse has. (4) 0260C CONFIRMED: 'Cor hominis ... os ejus, et labiis illius addet gratiam' against Pr 16:23 'Cor SAPIENTIS erudiet os ejus, et labiis EJUS addet gratiam'. ⚠ READING LEFT OPEN, 0260C: at 6x native the Gallica plate reads the verb as 'crudiet', a non-word, with no e before the r; the archive.org OCR text layer and our TEI both read 'erudiet'. An e losing its crossbar to read as c is the classic ink-loss shape, the archive copy is jbig2 symbol-substitution and cannot settle a letter, and a [sic:] is a public accusation. NO MARKER AND NO PATCH; the English carries the twin's 'erudiet'. Same disposition as the 0010-0014 stint's Greek at 0219B. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: '(Psl. iii)' at 0260A, MIGNE'S OWN misprint, with '(Psal. lvii)' printing correctly two lines below on the same column -- his, not ours, no patch; '(I Joan. v)', '(Psal. xviii.)', '(Luc. xix)'; 'super quinque mnas'; 'non percussorem (I Tim. iii)'; 'VERS. 29-36. -- Quod si bos cornupeta, etc. (RAB.)'.

reads.found: CHECKED ZERO at the foot of both columns, both apparatus layers. ONE [var:] SITE AND TWO CONFIRMATIONS THAT PREVENT PATCHES. (1) 0261D CONFIRMED: 'VERS. 25. -- Si pecunia mutuam, etc. (RAB.)' -- Migne prints the NOMINATIVE 'pecunia' with the accusative 'mutuam', which does not construe, where Ex 22:25 has 'Si pecuniam mutuam dederis'. Corroborated independently by the archive.org OCR text layer, which reads 'Si pecunia mutuamy etc.' -- so both witnesses agree the m is absent and this is not one photograph's ink. Marked [var:], not [sic:]: the type is legible and the words are real. (2) 0261C CONFIRMED: the Rabanus gloss on Ex 22:18 ends 'donec maleficium erroris in eis moriatur' WITH NO TERMINAL FULL STOP. Migne's own; Pattern 8 forbids supplying one and the English ends without a stop. (3) 0262A-B CONFIRMED: '(AUG., quaest, 86 in Exod.)' with a COMMA after quaest, where its neighbours on the same column print '(AUG., loc. 99.)' and '(GREG., lib. xvi Moral., cap. 2.)'. The comma is MIGNE'S and stands. What is OURS is that the TEI failed to mark this parenthetical as a note at all and left it as a bare italic span; filed as a markup patch. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: 'Maleficos non patieris vivere', 'Advenam non contristabis', 'Viduae et pupillo non nocebitis', 'Si pignus', 'Diis non detrahes', 'Decimas tuas' -- every VERS. lemma of chapter XXII agrees with the Clementine; 'Gratis accepistis, gratis date'; 'Sicut ovis ad occisionem ductus est (Isa. liii)', Is 53:7's future 'ducetur' against Migne's perfect, which is Acts 8:32's form -- declined.
